claims.evidence: The witness sees the housing and torque converter, but internal components, sensors, and solenoids are not visible or tested.
The witness report states the brand and model are unknown and no identification was read from the unit.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure or worn clutch packs.
risks.proof: A video of the transmission being tested on a bench or a clear photo of the internal fluid condition (checking for metal shavings).
risks.if_unproven: As a non-functional unit for parts/scrap only.

risks.risk: Faulty Transmission Control Unit (TCU) or conductor plate.
risks.proof: A diagnostic scan report showing no active fault codes for the solenoids or speed sensors.
risks.if_unproven: As having a failed electronic conductor plate.

risks.risk: Incorrect compatibility for M272 engine variants.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped part number or ID plate on the transmission casing (e.g., 722.9xx).
risks.if_unproven: As a generic, unidentified automatic transmission.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the identification plate or stamped serial numbers on the transmission casing.
Photo of the electrical connector pins to check for oil intrusion or damage.
A sample of the transmission fluid dropped onto a white cloth to check for burning or debris.
response.reason: The witness could not identify the brand or model. Without the identification plate to confirm it is a 722.9 series for an M272 engine, it is impossible to determine even a worst-case price for the correct vehicle application.
